title: Capacity Shepherding — weekly backlog & 1:1 prep
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Quick capture for my 1:1 with Ravi (ops lead) and weekly sync with Marina (product). Focus: keep pool runway > N weeks, validate reservation cadence, and unblock a short autoscale experiment.

Top goals for meeting:
1) Agree on headroom guardrail: keep 2.5x burst margin vs observed 95th percentile throughput across Tenant cohort A for next 6 weeks.
2) Decide whether to convert 40 ephemeral GPUs into a 3-month reservation starting Nov 1 as a runway hedge.
3) Finalize experiment plan to test gradual autoscale thresholds and cold-start latency measurement.

Quick data snapshot (as of 2024-10-03):
- Current dedicated pool total: 420 GPUs (A100-equivalent).
- Avg weekday peak consumption (10a–6p): 290 GPUs. 95p = 355 GPUs.
- Current unreserved (on-demand) capacity: 80 GPUs.
- Upcoming known commits: 50 GPUs reserved (Dec start) from Contract Z.
- Burn rate signal: steady +5% week-over-week for the last 3 weeks on training inference workloads.
- Prefetch/cache hit ratio improvement after prefix caching rollout: +12% token reduction (helps cost).

Scenario sketches (very rough):
- Conservative: assume 10% growth WoW — need 430 GPUs by mid-November. Reserve 60-80 GPUs Nov–Jan to avoid spot shortages.
- Base/Expected: 5% growth WoW — keep current reservations, rely on burst pool + autoscale to 1.3x.
- Aggressive: 15% growth WoW or a large customer onboarding — need immediate 100+ GPUs; fallback to cloud burst and emergency reservations (expensive).

Open questions / discussion items to surface:
- How much lead time does Infra really need to place a 90-180 day reservation? Can we start procurement in 2 weeks? (Owner: Ravi)
- Is there a contractual minimum for converting ephemeral capacity to reservation that affects pricing tiers? (Owner: Finance ops / Marina to check)
- Will enabling a lower autoscale threshold (CPU/GPU utilization 55% -> 45%) significantly increase cold-starts for model shards? Need A/B test. (Owner: Camille)

Experiment plan (lightweight, 3 weeks):
1) Week 0: Baseline capture — traffic replay small window (Mon 10–12), record cold-start p50/p95 for model families used in Dedicated.
2) Week 1: Lower autoscale threshold on a single pool (canary) from 55% to 45%, keep max burst constant. Monitor cold-start latency, error rates, and cost delta.
3) Week 2: If cold-start increase < 20% p95 and errors unchanged, scale to two pools. If not, rollback and document findings.
Metrics to capture: p50/p95 cold-start time, failed request rate, time-to-scale-up, cost per token delta, cache hit ratio.

Immediate action items (with quick owners & due dates):
- [Camille] Draft reservation proposal for 40 GPUs (3 months) with cost delta and break-even calc — due 2024-10-08.
- [Ravi] Confirm procurement lead time and if partial reservation (monthly commit) is possible — due 2024-10-10.
- [Marina] Check whether Contract Z terms block moving ephemeral GPUs to reserved pool earlier — due 2024-10-11.
- [Camille] Create canary config and rollout playbook for autoscale threshold experiment — due 2024-10-12.
- [Infra] Add alert for pool saturation at 80% of reserved capacity (to give ops 48h lead time) — requested 2024-10-04, ETA 2024-10-09.

Notes to self / talking points for 1:1:
- Emphasize runway risk: two >$1m customers onboarding in Nov would spike demand; want to avoid emergency rates.
- Tradeoff discussion: small reservations (30–50 GPUs) buy lead time and price predictability but reduce flexibility for experiment-driven bursts.
- Ask for a rough calendar: when will infra be occupied with other procurement so we can prioritize our reservation?

Meeting artifacts to produce after sync (post-meeting checklist):
- Short decision memo (1 page) summarizing chosen scenario and reservation ask (Camille).
- Updated pool forecast spreadsheet (include WoW growth sensitivity) — attach to Confluence (Ravi).
- GitHub PR with canary autoscale config and infra-as-code snippets (Camille).

Random brainstorm / long-list of mitigations if we can't reserve in time:
- Prioritize latency-sensitive tenants on reserved pools and routing others to hosted API.
- Employ stricter token limits for non-critical tenants during high-demand windows.
- Explore short-term cloud GPU burst from partner region (higher cost), reserve only minimal baseline.

Slack links / references to copy into meeting: #dedicated-capacity, #infra-procurement, relevant thread: slack-redwood-inference.slack.com/archives/C08J3QXKQ/p171305... (will paste exact link in meeting).

Status flags to watch next week:
- Reservation proposal accepted by finance?
- Autoscale canary results: success / rollback?
- New unexpected large commitment requests from Sales?

End notes: keep doc informal; will convert decision memo to Confluence once we have sign-off. Keep chasing procurement timelines — that is the main bottleneck.

Captured quickly, meant for my personal meeting prep. Will tidy after sync and move key outputs to shared drive.
